key_insight: THeatA simulations show that transport-induced heating can prevent logical errors from decreasing with code distance, while cooling ion pairs immediately before two-qubit gates can restore that scaling.
engineering_relevance: QCCD control and compiler design should account jointly for ion transport, motional heating, and cooling overhead rather than treating gate errors as fixed.
method: Compile syndrome-extraction circuits into an intermediate representation with QCCD-native transport and cooling operations.
Track per-ion mean phonon numbers and timing to generate gate-dependent noise in Stim circuits.
Evaluate rotated surface codes while sweeping cooling duration and post-cooling phonon number.
evidence_signal: Finite-size simulations identify cooling-parameter regions where logical error rates decrease with increasing code distance under the evaluated transport- and heating-aware noise conditions.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based for linear, single-species QCCD systems, and the abstract cooling instruction requires validation against realizable cooling protocols.
paper_title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
